subject: Geo-custody warranty & deletion SLAs for private VPC store
messages:
From: Jasmin Kaur <jasmin.kaur@helixhealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: security@helixhealth.com
Date: 2028-09-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Geo-custody warranty & deletion SLAs for private VPC store

Hi Olga,

We're evaluating Redwood Private for a patient-data workload and have a few governance questions before we move to procurement:

- Can Redwood provide a firm, contract-level guarantee that customer data stored in the private VPC (customer-controlled storage) will remain physically resident in the chosen AWS region and not be moved or replicated across regions without our approval?
- What is the timeline and evidence you can provide for a complete customer-initiated deletion (including keys, backups, and snapshots)? We need a maximum bounded time and an artifact we can retain for audit.
- For the case where we request a tenant handback and server wipe, can you provide an auditable attestation (signed by Redwood) that lists the erase steps and timestamps?
- Are there limitations where you would require additional lead time (e.g., cross-tenant maintenance windows, backup retention periods, or hardware decommissioning) that would affect the deletion SLA?

We'd like to include a short addendum to the contract with these commitments if possible. Can you share the operational playbook and a draft SLA addendum we could review?

Thanks,
Jasmin Kaur
Head of Cloud Security
Helix Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jasmin Kaur <jasmin.kaur@helixhealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-18T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Geo-custody warranty & deletion SLAs for private VPC store

Hi Jasmin — thanks for the clear list. I'm pulling our infra and compliance leads into thread so we can give you precise, auditable language. Quick high-level answers while we prepare the formal playbook: 

- Geo-binding: For Private (VPC) deployments where customer-managed storage is used, Redwood does not arbitrarily migrate tenant data across regions. We support region-locking and will include explicit contract language that disallows region replication without mutual consent.

- Deletion timeline: Typical full-erase timelines we operate to are: primary store deletion: within 24 hours of a verified request; snapshots/backups purge: up to 30 days depending on retention windows (we can negotiate shorter windows for contracted customers); KMS key destruction/zeroization: depends on key lifecycle and customer-managed keys (with CMK we can coordinate immediate rotation/revocation). We'll provide an attestation artifact with timestamps for each step.

- Attestation: We can provide a signed attestation that enumerates the steps taken (logical deletion, snapshot purge request, storage reclamation, KMS rotation/disablement) and timestamps. Template attestation is attached in the follow-up.

- Constraints: There are edge cases (e.g., cross-tenant deduplication on shared hardware, if enabled; hardware RMA requiring retention on encrypted drives pending secure erasure) — for Private deployments our default is tenant isolation that avoids these patterns; any residual constraints will be surfaced in the playbook and addendum.

I'll follow up this afternoon with the playbook and a draft SLA addendum. If you have a target acceptance timeline for the attestation (e.g., 30-day bound to final proof), let me know and we'll try to accommodate in the draft.

Best,
Olga
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-18T13:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Geo-custody warranty & deletion SLAs for private VPC store -- proposed playbook + SLA language (internal)

Team — forwarding Helix's questions. Draft below for discussion; I'm attaching a condensed playbook and an attestation template. Please review and reply with hard commitments we can sign to: 1) region-lock guarantee text, 2) end-to-end erase max windows, 3) attestation phrasing and signatory, 4) any exceptions/lead-time language.

Draft commitments (proposed):
- Region-binding: "Redwood will ensure Customer data in the Private VPC is logically and physically bound to the customer-selected AWS region(s). Redwood will not replicate or relocate Customer data to a different geographic region without prior written consent from the Customer, except as required by law."
- Erase timeline: "Upon a verified Customer deletion request, Redwood will: a) logically delete primary objects within 24 hours; b) action snapshot/archive purge requests within a maximum of 30 calendar days unless an alternate retention period is contractually agreed; c) initiate KMS key rotation or disablement as instructed; d) provide final storage reclamation confirmation within 45 calendar days."
- Attestation: "Redwood will provide a signed Erasure Attestation that documents the sequence of erase actions, timestamps, and operator IDs. The attestation will be delivered within 7 calendar days of final reclamation."
- Exceptions: Include a clause for hardware RMA or lawful holds that might extend timelines with notice to Customer.

Questions for the infra/compliance owners:
- Karthik: Are the 24/30/45 day bounds operationally realistic for all supported private deployment models (hosted private VPC, customer-managed storage, on-prem assisted wipe)? Any scenario that needs a longer bound?
- Priyom: Can we produce the signed attestation within 7 days of reclamation in the current workflow? What signatory should we use (Head of Infrastructure operations or Product Security)?
- Lauren: Legal wants minimal carve-outs — is the exceptions wording above defensible from a sales/enterprise contracting stance?

Attach: vpc_custody_playbook_v1.3.pdf, data_erase_attestation_template.docx, kms_key_rotation_summary.csv

Thanks,
Olga

Subject: Re: Geo-custody warranty & deletion SLAs for private VPC store

Hi Jasmin — thanks again for the clear list and patience while we pulled the team together. Attached is a condensed VPC custody playbook and a draft Erasure Attestation template for your review. Summary of formal commitments we can include in an SLA addendum: 

1) Region-binding warranty (contract language provided): Redwood warrants that Customer data in Private VPC deployments will remain resident in Customer-selected AWS region(s) and will not be replicated or moved to another region without Customer written consent, except where required by law.

2) Erase & evidence timeline (negotiable but our baseline): 
- Primary logical delete: within 24 hours of verified request
- Snapshots/backups purge: standard maximum 30 calendar days (can be shortened per contract)
- KMS key actions (for Redwood-managed keys): rotation/disablement initiated within 48 hours; for customer-managed CMKs, we coordinate immediate revocation as instructed
- Final storage reclamation confirmation: within 45 calendar days of request

3) Attestation: Redwood will deliver a signed Erasure Attestation that enumerates actions taken, timestamps, and operator IDs within 7 calendar days after final reclamation. The attestation will be signed by an authorized Redwood officer (Product Security Lead or Head of Infrastructure Operations) per customer preference.

4) Exceptions & lead time: We will include narrow, enumerated exceptions (e.g., lawful hold, cross-tenant dedupe if explicitly enabled, hardware RMA on encrypted drives) and commit to timely notification and mitigation plans. Any exception that would extend the schedule will be communicated with rationale and an expected completion date.

Next steps: 
- I've attached the playbook (vpc_custody_playbook_v1.3.pdf) and the attestation template (data_erase_attestation_template.docx) for your team to review.
- If this draft works, we can generate a short SLA addendum and route it for signature via DocuSign. Link to draft: https://docusign.com/signet/12345-SLA-addendum
- Please let me know if Helix requires a different signatory for the attestation (we can provide either Product Security Lead or Head of Infrastructure Ops).

Attachments: vpc_custody_playbook_v1.3.pdf (condensed operational steps), data_erase_attestation_template.docx (template attestation), kms_key_rotation_summary.csv (key lifecycle summary)

Looking forward to next steps — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through the playbook.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference
